draft.title: Factors affecting rate
card: The rate of a reaction is how fast reactants are used up or products form. A faster rate means more successful collisions each second.
Temperature
Higher temperature makes particles move faster, so they collide more often and more of them collide with enough energy.
Concentration and pressure
More particles in the same volume means more collisions each second. Raising the pressure of a gas does this by squeezing the same particles into a smaller volume.
Surface area and catalyst
Crushing a solid exposes more particles to collide with. A catalyst speeds up a reaction by giving it an easier path.
draft.remember: Each factor raises the number of successful collisions per second.

a.q: Why does a reaction speed up when a solution is made more concentrated?
opts: More particles in each volume, so more collisions per second
Each particle moves faster, so more have enough energy
Each particle gains energy, so every collision succeeds
The particles have a larger surface area to collide with
a.why: A higher concentration puts more reactant particles in the same volume, so collisions happen more often. Moving faster is the effect of a higher temperature, not of concentration.
a.clue: Think about how crowded the particles are.

b.q: Kofi reacts a 5 g lump of zinc with acid, then repeats it with 5 g of zinc powder. Nothing else changes. Why is the powder faster?
opts: More zinc particles are exposed to the acid
The zinc particles move faster in the acid
The acid becomes more concentrated
The zinc particles have more energy to start with
b.why: Powder has a much larger surface area, so more zinc particles can meet acid particles at once. The temperature and acid concentration are the same, so particle speed and energy are unchanged.
b.clue: The mass of zinc is the same, but how much of it is exposed?

a.best: More particles in each volume, so more collisions per second

b.best: More zinc particles are exposed to the acid
